claims.text: A neural network potential can improve representation of atomic configurations in the ab initio liquid of multicomponent high-entropy alloys.
Improved liquid-configuration representation by an NNP will reduce thermodynamic-integration path mismatch relative to TOR-TILD's EAM references.
Machine-learning-based NNPs can capture the complex atomic interactions present in high-entropy alloys.
The proposed method applies to alloys containing 3-6 principal elements.
The proposed method applies over the temperature range 0.8-1.2 T_m.
Improved representation of atomic interactions allows the NNP to capture the complex configurations of the ab initio liquid.
The NNP will reduce thermodynamic-integration path mismatch by at least 30% relative to TOR-TILD's EAM references.
Reducing thermodynamic-integration path mismatch will produce more accurate reference-target phase-space overlap.
NNP accuracy may depend on the quality and quantity of its training data.
NNP accuracy may depend on the selected machine-learning algorithm and hyperparameters.
The NNP can be benchmarked by comparing its calculated solid-liquid free-energy difference with ab initio molecular-dynamics results.
A deviation greater than 10% between the NNP-based free-energy calculation and the ab initio molecular-dynamics benchmark falsifies the hypothesis.
